newsitem.title: GERMANY: PWA first quarter pretax profit down, but improvements seen.
newsitem.headline: PWA first quarter pretax profit down, but improvements seen.

text.p: German paper manufacturer PWA Papierwerke Waldhof Aschaffenburg AG said on Tuesday that its pretax profit for the first quarter of 1997 fell to 70 million marks ($40 million) from 85 million previously, but said it expected substantial improvements over the year.

PWA said its first quarter pre-tax profit included 15 million marks in costs for a restructuring of its hygiene products business, a move which would produce its first substantial improvement in 1997.
The firm added that the year-earlier profit included one-off income of 46 million marks from the sale of plastics subsidiary PWA Kunststoff.

Operating profit, which excluded these special effects, was 90 million marks in the first quarter of 1996 versus 52 million previously, but compared with the final quarter of 1996, operating profit rose 48 percent, PWA said.
For 1996, PWA said its group net profit was 227 million marks, up from 163 million in 1995, and profit per share according to DVFA accounting rules dropped to 21 marks compared with 25 marks in 1995.
Profit from ordinary operations rose to 267 million marks in 1996 from 161 million previously, while cash flow stood at 497 million marks, up from 410 million in 1995.
The firm said its proposed dividend for 1996 would be seven marks per share, unchanged from 1995's levels.
